scheme_name: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation Fast Track
overview: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) Fast Track scheme is designed to expedite regulatory processes for pharmaceutical products, including drugs, biologics, and medical devices, by streamlining approvals, reducing timelines, and enhancing transparency in the evaluation and licensing procedures. It aims to facilitate faster market access for innovative and essential medical products while maintaining stringent safety, efficacy, and quality standards. The scheme leverages digital platforms like the SUGAM portal for online submissions and integrates with national regulatory frameworks to ensure uniformity and accountability across central and state drug control organizations.
objectives: Expedite approval processes for new drugs, biologics, and medical devices
Ensure uniform implementation of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and associated rules
Enhance transparency, accountability, and efficiency in regulatory services
Facilitate faster market access for essential and innovative medical products
Strengthen coordination between central and state drug control organizations
Promote adoption of digital systems like SUGAM for seamless submission and tracking
Ensure safety, efficacy, and quality of medical products manufactured, imported, and distributed in India
eligibility: Eligibility applies to manufacturers, importers, exporters, and authorized agents of drugs, biologics, medical devices, and cosmetics seeking registration, import licensing, or market authorization in India. Applicants must comply with the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and Rules 1945, including submission of required documentation via the SUGAM portal, adherence to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Distribution Practices (GDP), and provision of valid wholesale/manufacturing licenses, product details, stability data, and undertakings as specified in CDSCO guidelines. Startups and MSMEs may avail relaxations in experience and turnover criteria under relevant government policies.
benefits: Faster processing of registration certificates, import licenses, and market authorizations; reduced timelines for scrutiny and approval via digital SUGAM portal; enhanced transparency through online tracking and status updates; facilitation of export-oriented permissions and no-objection certificates; support for innovation via accelerated pathways for biologics and medical devices; alignment with international regulatory standards; access to guidance documents, public notices, and stakeholder consultation mechanisms; and integration with national pharmacovigilance and quality control systems.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers procedural and regulatory benefits including fee-based services (e.g., application fees for registration and import licensing), with costs borne by applicants. Financial transactions are processed via TR-6 challans for fees deposited under relevant heads (e.g., '0210 - Medical and Public Health'). No corpus fund or per-entity financial allocation is specified under this fast track mechanism.
application_process: 1. Access the SUGAM portal at https://sugam.cdsco.in for online submission. 2. Determine the appropriate application form (e.g., Form 40 for Registration Certificate, Form 8/8A for Import License) based on the product type. 3. Prepare and upload required documents including covering letter, application form, power of attorney, TR-6 challan of fees paid, import permissions, wholesale/manufacturing licenses, authorization letters, product specifications, stability data, and labels. 4. Submit the application through the SUGAM portal. 5. Undergo technical review by Drugs Inspector, Assistant Drugs Inspector, Assistant Drugs Controller, Deputy Drugs Controller, and Joint Drugs Controller. 6. Respond to any queries raised during review. 7. Receive final approval or rejection from the Drug Controller General of India (for Registration Certificate) or Joint Drugs Controller (for Import License). 8. Upon approval, download the certificate or license from the portal.
required_documents: Covering Letter indicating type of application
Application in Form-40 (for Registration Certificate) or Form 8/8A (for Import License)
TR-6 Challan of fees paid (1500 USD per site or equivalent in INR; 1000 USD per drug or equivalent)
Copy of Import permission for new drug (Form-45 or Form-45A)
Copy of Valid Wholesale License (20B/21C) or Manufacturing License of Indian agent
Notarised copy of Plant Master File (PMF)
Notarised copy of Drug Master File (DMF)
Original Notarised Copy of Manufacturing Licence, FSC, GMP, COPP (for finished products)
Attested/Appostilled copy of Product Registration Certificate (e.g., CFDA, EDQM)
Original label/specimen label complying with Rule 96, indicating subject drug with pharmacopoeial specification, importer name & address, and Import License number
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round via the SUGAM portal with no fixed annual deadline.
implementing_agency: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
caveats: Applications are subject to strict scrutiny; deficiencies may lead to rejection or requests for compliance
Approval is contingent upon meeting all regulatory requirements under Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules 1945
The fast track process does not compromise on safety, efficacy, or quality standards
EMD exemption available for MSMEs and DPIIT-recognized startups under GeM GTC for tender-related services
Guidelines for similar biologics and medical devices are subject to periodic revision; applicants must refer to latest versions
Post-approval changes require separate submission via SUGAM portal
